rebaseCheck.verdict: changed, so a full test round was run
rebaseCheck.why: Besides the 17 fragments renamed to pr2390-* (no INFRA- text remains in packages/*/.changes/unreleased/) and docs merged with main's #2368, the merge changed code: store.ConnectionsPerProcess adds registryPoolSize = 1 (85 in all), infra/gcp dispatchConnectionsPerPod goes from 83 to 85, and main's /livez is served beside this change's /healthz.

implementerProof.how: Rebuilt every binary at 75c172e2 and drove each surface of the implementer's proofs independently with the tester's own harness, on Postgres 17.5 and natsd: NATS-down boot and publish, cross-process sign-in with refresh, the refusals and the admission wait, the dev restart after SIGKILL, freeze and database-cut resume, issuer-down boot, the announcement roll and BuildCommit. It also checked the merge's additions: the real process's Postgres connection count against ConnectionsPerProcess, and /livez during outages.

ci: At 75c172e2, read at 10:50Z: test, typecheck, lint, build (x2), changes and pr-title queued (one pr-title run cancelled). Read as queued, not as a pass. GitHub reports MERGEABLE.

proof.criterion: Merge resolution: a process stays within the per-process connection budget that now counts the registry's pool; /livez stays independent of the dependencies
proof.surface: the real envoy-dispatch at the head with NATS connected, its database's pg_stat_activity; /livez with NATS down, with the database cut through a TCP proxy, and during the admission wait
proof.command: tester's harness: count pg_stat_activity backends for the process's database at idle and every 50 ms during 1500 GET /api/v1/projects, 150 concurrent; curl /livez in each outage
proof.observed: 10 connections at idle; peak 71 under load, all 200, within ConnectionsPerProcess = 85 (64+4+1+11+1+1+3); /livez 204 with NATS down and with the database cut (/healthz 503 then 200); no /livez answer during the admission wait, which the app's 30-minute startup probe (answersProbe(8766, 10, 180)) covers
proof.negativeControl: the database cut made /healthz answer 503 while /livez kept 204, so the probe that may restart a pod does not read Postgres

proof.criterion: A process started while NATS is unreachable becomes healthy (/healthz 200, nats false) and serves an API read; once NATS is reachable it reports nats true and publishes
proof.surface: real envoy-dispatch stamped 75c172e2 on Postgres 17.5 (schema 135), natsd from the head
proof.command: tester's harness: boot with NATS_URLS at an unused port, /healthz, API read, relay, start natsd, read notifications.dispatch.server.started, SIGSTOP natsd
proof.observed: /healthz 200 nats:false 1.0 s after start; API 200; relay 503; nats:true 0.25 s after natsd started; one envelope ...-75c172e2...-1; silent cut shown in 2.53 s
proof.negativeControl: b08a56bc with NATS down: exit 1 at boot

proof.criterion: A sign-in started on A completes on B; a key rotation keeps people signed in; a process with no key or an unshared key set does not serve, also on resume
proof.surface: two real envoy-dispatch processes ("K1 K0"/"K0 K1") with dev-oidc-issuer; a third beside them; A on KX frozen or cut 17 s with B started meanwhile; a dev sign-in server SIGKILLed and restarted
proof.command: tester's harness: A /auth/start -> issuer -> B callback, whoami both, bad state cookies, refresh on A then B, A-minted cookie to B; K9, unset and 'K1 K0' beside the pair; SIGTERM 4 s into the wait; freeze/cut scenarios; dev restart; empty signing-key file
proof.observed: B callback 302, whoami 200 on both; bad state cookies 400 x3; refresh re-seals on both; A's cookie 200 on B; K9 and unset exit 1 after 20.3 s; 'K1 K0' serves; SIGTERM in the wait exits 0; B=KY: A exits 1 (0.3 s after the freeze, 2.8 s after the cut ends); B=KX both serve; dev restart serves after 15.6 s; empty key file exits 1 naming it
proof.negativeControl: b08a56bc: B's callback 400 and K9 serves beside the pair; 0b7f2af5: frozen A beside B=KY resumes and both serve with both rows live

proof.criterion: A process started while the discovery document is unreachable serves agent-token requests and completes a sign-in once discovery succeeds
proof.surface: real envoy-dispatch with both issuers at a SIGSTOPped dev-oidc-issuer
proof.command: tester's harness: boot frozen; /healthz, agent token, JWT, /auth/start; SIGCONT; poll; JWT; sign-in; refresh during a second freeze
proof.observed: 200 signin:false service_tokens:false; agent token 200; JWT 503 OIDC_ISSUER_UNAVAILABLE; /auth/start 503 SIGNIN_UNAVAILABLE; recovered in 7 s; JWT 200; sign-in 302, whoami 200; refresh during the outage 503, then 200
proof.negativeControl: b08a56bc with the issuer frozen: exit 1

proof.criterion: A test of the started-event contract on both sides
proof.surface: two real envoy-dispatch processes stamped c1/c2 on one Postgres and natsd; the daemon's HTTPClient.BuildCommit against a live c1 process
proof.command: tester's harness: roll c1 -> c2 -> rollback, reading the stream and fleet_commit after each step; a temporary go test calling New(url).BuildCommit (deleted after the run)
proof.observed: envelopes (c1,1), none, none (fleet_commit c1 on both mid-roll), (c2,2), (c1,3); BuildCommit returned c1c1...

residualRisks: The state cookie can be replayed for its 10 minutes; only the issuer's single-use code stops a second callback.
A request whose confirmation has lapsed waits for the refresh timeout (about 15 s) while the issuer does not answer, then answers 503.
A process refused at boot holds its bound port without serving (and without answering /livez) for up to about 20 s before it exits; the app's startup probe covers that window.
